page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores with hyperthreading, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8252C processor running at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

In benchmark testing, the x2iezn.12xlarge demonstrates strong memory performance, scoring in the top 25% for Passmark memory tests and large-block memory bandwidth, with 209.78 GB/sec read and 98.02 GB/sec write speeds. Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 31.81 GB/sec. However, CPU-bound tasks like stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core fall into the average tier. LLM text generation performance is weak, with the 7B model achieving only 7.82 tokens/sec, highlighting a tradeoff where the instance excels in memory capacity and bandwidth but is limited in compute-heavy parallel processing compared to GPU-accelerated alternatives.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, making it highly optimized for network and EBS throughput. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density and high-frequency Intel Xeon cores position this instance as a specialized resource for memory-intensive workloads that also require fast single-core execution. It is best suited for large in-memory databases, enterprise applications, high-performance electronic design automation, and memory-bound data processing pipelines.
